# Tic-Tac-Toe: Proposed Canon Draft r1

Status: in-progress; readiness: not-assessed. This is a partial candidate set, not admitted Canon, a complete proposal, or permission to implement. All candidate keys below are local to this capture; each is revision 1 with disposition add. There are no predecessor candidates. The maintained owner is ADHOC-7fd789738d5348cbbbd4f4cb378fbecf, workflow.planning, request tic-tac-toe-canon-r1. The JSON request is a retained input, not a second maintained specification.

## Source Inventory And Reconciliation

The entire selected corpus consists of three sources. All three were considered for requirements, definitions, acceptance direction and conflicts; none was excluded or only inventoried.
- source-1: original feature request, assistant proposals, Operator confirmation and answers. SHA-256 d6139844ec225d1e36ddd07d9552bc8aa1a64fc14a38fc6b935560f49bea69ed. Explicit: React, 0-2 human players, unbeatable AI and human mark choice. Conventional game rules and browser-only/shared-device scope were assistant interpretations.
- source-2: confirmed manual replay decision. SHA-256 7af814bf2cd85e7440edec3184c9e505435e77ebf8d7fad2359c3b2ed884e961. Resolves source-1's replay ambiguity for AI-vs-AI without rewriting source-1.
- source-3: confirmed Node.js/Express local port 3630 and desktop/mobile browser requirements. SHA-256 3546cbb855ed4253554279579fe77387fb3eaccfe03310fe79b5f2db2e44e616. Narrows the earlier browser-only suggestion: browser UI does not mean absence of an Express server.

## Proposed Definitions

Each definition below is proposed product vocabulary, scoped only to this game and owned by this draft r1. None changes installed control-plane terminology.
- d-human-count (definition): human-player count is the number of human-controlled marks in a game: 0, 1 or 2. The source's '0 players' means zero HUMAN players, not an empty board with nobody playing; X and O still exist. Source: source-1. No other aliases asserted.
- d-ai (definition): AI is the computer-controlled opponent/player. 'Unbeatable' means it never loses from a fresh legal game against any sequence of legal opponent moves, whether it controls X or O. A draw is valid; unbeatable does not mean winning every game. Two such AIs draw under standard rules. Source: source-1; this formalizes the conventional meaning, not an external AI service or a selected algorithm.
- d-game (definition): one game is a standard 3x3 round from an empty board until an X win, O win or draw. 'Round' is a proposed explanatory synonym, not evidence of a broader match/scoring feature. Source: source-1 and conventional tic-tac-toe rules. A game is distinct from the browser session; no multi-game score is implied.
- d-replay (definition): 'Play again' is the user-triggered action that begins another game after a terminal result. In zero-human mode a person can trigger replay without controlling either mark. Source: source-2. No automatic-repeat meaning is permitted.

## Proposed Requirements And Acceptance Direction

- r-rules (requirement; source-1; conventional rules elaboration): use nine cells in a 3x3 board, with X first and turns alternating X/O. A move places exactly one mark in an empty cell. Three identical marks in any row, column or diagonal wins; a full board with no winner draws. A winning final move takes precedence over a draw. No moves occur after termination. Acceptance: cover all eight winning lines for both marks, a draw, occupied-cell rejection, turn order and terminal immutability. Uses d-game@r1.
- r-modes (requirement; source-1; explicit): support 0 humans (AI controls both marks), 1 human (human versus AI), and 2 humans (human controls each mark in turn). Human clicks/taps cannot place moves for an AI-controlled turn. Acceptance: play a complete game in each mode; verify zero-human games advance without board input and two-human games have no autonomous moves. Uses d-human-count@r1 and r-rules@r1. Shared-device play is the working scope, subject to the assumptions below.
- r-mark-choice (requirement; source-1; explicit): before a one-human game, let the human choose X or O and assign the other mark to the AI. Acceptance: choosing X gives the human the opening move; choosing O causes the AI to open as X. Uses r-rules@r1 and r-modes@r1.
- r-unbeatable (requirement; source-1; explicit with testable interpretation): every AI-controlled mark satisfies d-ai@r1. Acceptance: systematically explore all legal human move sequences from a fresh game for both AI mark choices and demonstrate zero AI losses; verify every chosen move is legal. If AI tie-breaking is nondeterministic, verification must cover every permitted choice rather than one favorable run. AI-vs-AI terminates in a draw. Algorithm/library choice remains implementation work. This does not promise a win against perfect play.
- r-result (requirement; source-1 proposed turn/result display, source-2 confirmed result retention): show whose turn it is during play and an unambiguous X win, O win or draw at termination. Retain the finished board and result while waiting for replay. Acceptance: labels agree with the board, and waiting after AI-vs-AI finishes does not clear it or schedule a new game. Uses r-rules@r1 and d-replay@r1.
- r-manual-replay (requirement; source-2; explicit for AI-vs-AI): provide a button labelled 'Play again' after the game. AI-vs-AI must wait for a person to activate it before another game begins. Activation clears the previous game's board/result and starts a single new game with X first. Acceptance: no automatic repeat after any waiting period; one activation creates one fresh game and no delayed move from the prior game appears in it. Applying this same control to all modes and retaining mode/mark settings are recommendations below, not additional source assertions. Uses d-replay@r1 and r-rules@r1.
- r-react (requirement; source-1; explicit): implement the interactive application in React. Acceptance: the actual delivered browser application uses React for its game interface, not an unrelated standalone implementation. No bundler or language beyond the selected framework is prescribed here.
- r-runtime (requirement; source-3; explicit): run locally with Node.js and Express serving the React application at port 3630. Acceptance: with the local server running, the application loads and completes a game through that port. Port 3630 is the requirement; silently falling back to another port is not equivalent. Recommend reporting an actionable startup error if it is occupied. Versions, start command and serving/build details are to be specified during work planning.
- r-browsers (requirement; source-3; explicit with usability interpretation): the game must run in both desktop and mobile browsers with a responsive layout and usable controls. Acceptance: on selected desktop and mobile targets, the full board, mode and mark controls, turn/result display and Play again remain accessible without overlap or clipping; pointer and touch input both work, and the game rules do not change with viewport size. Exact browser/version and viewport coverage remains a proposed validation matrix, not verified support.

## Proposed User Stories

- s-solo (story; source-1): as a human, I choose my mark and play standard tic-tac-toe against an unbeatable AI. Satisfied by r-rules@r1, r-modes@r1, r-mark-choice@r1, r-unbeatable@r1 and r-result@r1.
- s-watch (story; sources 1-2): as an observer, I watch two unbeatable AIs complete a game and decide when to start another using Play again. Satisfied by r-modes@r1, r-unbeatable@r1, r-result@r1 and r-manual-replay@r1. Visible pacing is recommended below.
- s-two-humans (story; source-1): as two local participants, we alternate legal moves and see the result. Satisfied by r-rules@r1, r-modes@r1 and r-result@r1; same-device use is the working interpretation.
- s-local-browser (story; sources 1 and 3): as a user, I access the React game served by local Express on port 3630 from a desktop or mobile browser. Satisfied by r-react@r1, r-runtime@r1 and r-browsers@r1. Physical-device connectivity is an open setup decision, not a networked-multiplayer requirement.

## Recommendations And Remaining Assumptions

These proposed defaults are not recorded Operator decisions and need confirmation before a complete proposal relies on them.
- a-session: one game per browser session on a shared device; no accounts, networked multiplayer, database, persistent scores, saved games, difficulty levels or external AI service. These keep the requested simple scope; adding any is a scope decision. Refresh may return to setup rather than restore a game.
- a-replay: use the same manual Play again behavior in all three modes, retaining the selected mode and human mark between games. Setup changes apply to a new game, never silently change control mid-turn. Recommend allowing mode/mark changes only before the first move or after a terminal result for this version.
- a-pacing: show each AI move separately, with a proposed 500 ms delay before each AI turn, including the opening AI move. This makes AI-vs-AI observable; exact timing was not specified. Timer delays may be longer in background tabs; correctness must not depend on exact elapsed time.
- a-compatibility: propose current stable Chrome/Firefox/Safari for desktop and Safari on iOS plus Chrome on Android, with representative 1280x800 desktop and 390x844 mobile checks, plus a narrow 320px-width layout check. Browser versions at verification must be recorded; this is a recommendation, not a current pass. Keyboard-operable cells/buttons and visible focus are also recommended without claiming an accessibility certification.
- a-connectivity: distinguish a desktop's local server from a phone's localhost. For a physical phone, use an explicitly chosen same-LAN host address/binding and port 3630; do not expose the server publicly by inference. Alternatively, mobile emulation checks layout but does not establish physical-device/browser operation. Confirm the intended access and acceptance scope.

## Risks, Rework And Dependencies

An overly weak AI check can falsely claim unbeatable behavior; systematic legal-tree verification addresses this. Stale asynchronous AI actions can alter a finished or restarted game; acceptance must cover those cases. Rendering all AI moves at once undermines observation even when rules are correct; a-pacing proposes a remedy. Desktop-only testing cannot establish mobile-browser behavior. Local serving and LAN reachability need separate verification.

All candidates are proposed additions without fabricated existing Canon identities. No product implementation, completed-phase evidence or admitted base has been examined because this pass is source-backed drafting and no operational baseline was supplied. This is not evidence of absence of historical implementation or a finding of nonconformance. Before completing a proposal, reconcile the actual selected baseline, implementation and execution state and report affected work honestly. No phase is reopened.

Requirements refer to local definition/requirement revisions above; these are semantic relationships, not execution DAG edges. Work shaping is a separate operation. No phases, trackers or execution edges are added, removed or reordered by this draft. React delivery, Express serving and browser verification are required scope, not preselected phase boundaries. No reviewed subject exists here to carry forward as approval.

## Representation And Next Boundary

Only definition, requirement and story candidate kinds are used. Detailed acceptance cases, attribution, semantic relationships and assumptions are retained in draft text; they are not new structured kernel fields. No schema extension is requested. Original sources and their histories remain intact; resolving an ambiguity in this synthesis does not rewrite them or manufacture a SCRUB disposition.

Next: Operator review of this draft and its recommended defaults, then separately authorized work shaping. A complete proposal later requires an explicit operational base/execution snapshot and resolution of affected assumptions. Formal review, approval, publication, integration and product start remain separate boundaries.
questions: Confirm the simple shared-device/session scope in a-session, including no persistence or networked multiplayer; these originated as assistant proposals.
Confirm manual replay in all modes, retention of mode/mark settings, and setup changes only before play or after termination (a-replay).
Confirm the proposed 500 ms AI-turn pacing, including the first AI move (a-pacing).
Confirm the browser/viewport validation matrix and whether physical-phone access over the local network is required rather than emulation alone (a-compatibility and a-connectivity).
Before complete proposal/admission, select the real destination and operational baseline/execution snapshot; do not silently admit the tic-tac-toe test feature into PokerNight product scope.
